message.content: The number of distinct positions that can arise in a game of chess is astronomically large – on the order of **10⁴³** (roughly 100 000 000 000 000 000 000 000 000 000 000 000 000). This estimate, often called the Shannon number, gives a sense of the sheer combinatorial complexity of the game.
